text:
olivia: Quick follow-up from today's RFC review: observed churn when applying delta bundles over flaky links. operator retries end up re-downloading the same large blobs repeatedly.
raj: do we have retry-idempotency? operator should dedupe on blob checksum but sounds like retries are restarting partial streams.
marta: operator currently writes blobs to temp paths like `.part-<blobid>` and renames on completion. retries overwrite the .part file and velocity is terrible with small MTU.
simon: idea: introduce resumable transfer tokens + byte-range resume for blobs. packager would publish blob-length + chunk-hash list so operator can resume at chunk N.
jena: that's fine but for airgapped/drifted mirrors we also need a compact manifest that lists critical service binaries first (boot-critical) and low-priority model shards later. operator can apply in two phases: boot-critical then background.
olivia: agree on phased apply. also propose a small transactional model: write-ahead manifest (WAM) that lists apply steps; operator checkpoints progress to WAM so rollback on failure is deterministic.
raj: WAM + signed checkpoints could also help attestation: customer can prove which manifest was activated and which blobs were skipped. do we sign checkpoints with KMS?
marta: sign the WAM root and each checkpoint hash chain. verifier only needs to trust root signature. This avoids re-signing every checkpoint.
simon: implementation note: WAM must include pre/post hooks: prefetch list, extraction order, activation sentinel path. operator should expose `--resume-from-checkpoint <id>`.
jena: for low-bandwidth sites let's add a priority flag on blobs (`priority: high|medium|low`) and a `prefetch_window` in manifest. packager will emit prioritized index first so operator can fetch critical small blobs synchronously and stream large low-priority ones with throttle.
olivia: also ran into mixed-compat when packager compresses with zstd-level 19 — some old tar extractors choke. packager should set compatibility defaults and include `compression: zstd:level=3` in manifest metadata.
raj: good catch. Also need a change to delta application: when applying a delta that deletes files, operator must record delete list in WAM so rollback can undelete from retained previous activation. garbage collection policy must retain at least one prior activation and associated blobs.
marta: GC policy: retain N=1 previous activation by default, configurable. operator should fail activation if previous fails retention requirement.
simon: testing: add an e2e scenario: pause network midway through large-blob stream and assert operator resumes and final checksum matches manifest. this should be part of packaging-e2e.
ci-bot: CI: packaging-e2e scenario "resume-chunked-download" queued on branch "rfc/delta-resume" — job 7892.
jena: minor UX: console should show per-blob progress with priority tags and `estimated_time_remaining`. customers asked for visibility when transferring to remote airgap couriers.
olivia: security question: resumable tokens could leak info about blob sizes. ensure tokens are short-lived and opaque; prefer chunk-index lists over server-issued tokens when offline.
raj: agree. packager publishes chunk-hash list signed in manifest; operator resumes by referencing the signed chunk sequence. no live token needed.
marta: action items: (1) packager: emit chunked-index + priority + compression metadata (owner: olivia), (2) operator: implement WAM + resume CLI + phased apply (owner: simon), (3) verifier: trust signed chunk lists and checkpoint chain (owner: raj), (4) infra: add e2e resume tests and low-bandwidth rehearsal harness (owner: jena).
simon: I'll prototype WAM format: json-lines events with fields `step_id`, `action`, `blob_id`, `byte_range`, `status`, `prev_hash`. simple to append and verify.
jena: for rehearsals we'll spin an LXC-based limited-bandwidth mirror to emulate couriers. I'll post setup notes in #eng-oncall once ready.
olivia: I'll include these in the RFC addendum and draft manifest schema snippets. will tag reviewers. thx all :rocket:
